question.prompt:
A triangle is partitioned into three triangles and a quadrilateral by drawing two lines from vertices to their opposite sides. The areas of the three triangles are \(3,\) \(7,\) and \(7,\) as shown. What is the area of the shaded quadrilateral?

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_10B_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Label the bottom left, bottom right, and top vertices \(A,B,C\), respectively. Let \(D\) be the endpoint on \(AC\), \(E\) the endpoint on \(BC\), and \(P\) the intersection of the drawn segments \(AE\) and \(BD\). Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). The figure gives
\[
[APD]=3,\qquad [APB]=[BPE]=7.
\]
The two area-7 triangles have bases \(AP\) and \(PE\) on the same line and share the altitude from \(B\). Since triangle area is half the product of base and height, their equal areas imply \(AP=PE\).

Draw \(CP\). Because \(P\) is the midpoint of \(AE\), this median divides triangle \(CAE\) into equal-area triangles \(CAP\) and \(CEP\): their bases \(AP\) and \(PE\) are equal and they share the altitude from \(C\).

Let \(x=[CPD]>0\). Triangle \(CAP\) consists of triangles \(CPD\) and \(APD\), so
\[
[CAP]=[CEP]=x+3.
\]
It follows that
\[
[CPB]=[CPE]+[EPB]=x+10.
\]
Now triangles \(APD\) and \(APB\) share the altitude from \(A\) to line \(BD\), giving \(PD:PB=3:7\). Triangles \(CPD\) and \(CPB\) have these same bases and share the altitude from \(C\). Therefore,
\[
x=\frac37(x+10),
\qquad 7x=3x+30,
\qquad x=\frac{15}{2}.
\]
The shaded quadrilateral \(CDPE\) consists of triangles \(CPD\) and \(CPE\), so its area is
\[
x+(x+3)=2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)+3=\boxed{18}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Equal areas reveal a midpoint
